findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow uses independent String status, bool is_validated, bool is_sent fields instead of typed enums or a typestate. Illegal states are trivially representable (e.g. status='sent' with is_sent=false, or status='created' with is_sent=true).
findings.failure_mode: Any caller or mutation can place LeaseWorkflow into an inconsistent state that the type system cannot catch, violating the core DDD invariant that illegal states are unrepresentable.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a sealed enum LeaseStatus { Created, Sent } and remove is_validated/is_sent bools. Use a typestate pattern: LeaseWorkflow<LeaseStatus::Created> cannot be used where LeaseStatus::Sent is required without going through a fallible transition.

findings.problem: All fields of LeaseWorkflow are pub, so any code outside the module can construct invalid states directly (e.g. LeaseWorkflow { id: "x", status: "foo", is_validated: true, is_sent: true, sent_at_epoch_ms: None }).
findings.failure_mode: No constructor enforces invariants; the struct is a mutable bag of primitives with no domain guarantees at any call site.
findings.fix: Make all fields private, provide a fallible constructor that validates invariants, and replace primitive types with domain newtypes/enums.

findings.problem: status: String is a primitive string instead of a typed domain enum. The ubiquitous language (created/sent/completed) is encoded as magic strings.
findings.failure_mode: Typos, unknown status values, case sensitivity bugs, and impossible-to-audit state transitions at every call site that reads or writes status.
findings.fix: Replace with enum LeaseStatus { Created, Sent } (or similar domain-accurate variants). Use `match` on the enum instead of string comparison.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw string instead of a typed LeaseId newtype. No domain validation or semantic guarantee on the id value.
findings.failure_mode: Any string (empty, whitespace, malformed) can be used as a lease ID, causing downstream bugs that are hard to trace back to the source.
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct LeaseId(String)` with a fallible constructor (or FromStr impl) and use LeaseId instead of String in LeaseWorkflow.

findings.problem: All five fields of LeaseWorkflow are declared pub, exposing internal representation and allowing unvalidated mutation from any crate.
findings.failure_mode: Direct field mutation bypasses any transition invariants, making it impossible to enforce lifecycle ordering or audit state changes.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide transition methods (e.g. fn mark_sent(self) -> Result<LeaseWorkflow<Sent>, Error>) and a constructor.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes and returns the same LeaseWorkflow type. Without typestates, there is no compile-time guarantee that the lease was in a valid pre-sent state before marking. The function can be called on an already-sent or never-created lease indistinguishably.
findings.failure_mode: Idempotent or out-of-order transitions are not prevented by the type system. Business logic bugs (double-sending, sending without creation) are runtime errors instead of compile errors.
findings.fix: Use a typestate pattern: `fn mark_sent(self) -> LeaseWorkflow<Sent>` where the input type enforces the pre-condition (e.g. only `LeaseWorkflow<Created>` can be passed). Alternatively, at minimum, have mark_sent return `Result<LeaseWorkflow, TransitionError>` with a guard check.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool encode lifecycle state. Per the reference, bool lifecycle flags should be replaced with enums or typestates.
findings.failure_mode: Booleans only encode two states and cannot express multi-way transitions (e.g. validated vs not validated vs pending validation). Combined with the String status field, there is redundancy and contradiction surface.
findings.fix: Replace with typed enums or a single typestate enum. If validation is a separate concern, use a separate enum field or nested typestate.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> stores milliseconds since epoch as raw u64. No newtype wrapper or checked conversion at parse boundaries. No documentation or constraint on what constitutes a valid timestamp.
findings.failure_mode: Without a typed wrapper, callers may confuse milliseconds with seconds/nanoseconds. At parse boundaries (deserialization from external sources), unchecked conversions can produce invalid or misinterpreted timestamps.
findings.fix: Introduce `struct TimestampMs(u64)` with a fallible constructor and use it in LeaseWorkflow. Add documentation for the epoch convention.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates the struct in place and returns it (`.to_string()` allocation on line 10). This is a thin imperative wrapper, but the struct itself is not a pure data type because it lacks invariants enforced by the type system.
findings.failure_mode: The function appears pure but allocates (`.to_string()`) and mutates, mixing pure and imperative concerns. If this grows to include I/O (e.g. persistence), the functional boundary would be violated silently.
findings.fix: Make mark_sent a pure function that returns a new validated LeaseWorkflow instance. Move any I/O (sending notifications, persisting) to a separate shell-layer action function.

residual_risk: High. The entire domain model is built on primitive types with no type-level invariants. Every call site is free to construct illegal states, making the system vulnerable to silent business logic errors. Typestate enforcement, domain newtypes, and private fields are mandatory fixes. Static review only; no commands run.
